hints: Separate the variables by dividing by $x$ and multiplying by $dt$.
Rewrite $\sqrt t$ as $t^{1/2}$ before integrating both sides.
Include a constant of integration in the relation containing $\ln x$ and $t^{3/2}$.
Use the initial condition $t=0$, $x=100$ to determine that constant.
walkthrough:
Separate variables in the differential equation $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = -kx\sqrt{t}$:
$$\dfrac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x = -k\sqrt{t}\,\mathrm{d}t = -kt^{\frac{1}{2}}\,\mathrm{d}t$$

Integrate both sides:
$$\int \dfrac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x = \int -kt^{\frac{1}{2}}\,\mathrm{d}t$$
$$\ln x = -k\left(\dfrac{t^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\frac{3}{2}}\right) + C = -\dfrac{2}{3}kt^{\frac{3}{2}} + C$$

Use the initial condition $x = 100$ when $t = 0$:
$$\ln 100 = -\dfrac{2}{3}k(0) + C \implies C = \ln 100$$

Write the final relation between $x$, $t$, and $k$:
$$\ln x = -\dfrac{2}{3}kt\sqrt{t} + \ln 100$$

hints: Use the integrated relation from part (i) for both stated conditions.
Substitute $t=25$ and $x=80$ to obtain an equation involving $k$.
Write a second equation by setting $x=40$ and denoting the required time by $t$.
Eliminate $k$, solve for $t^{3/2}$, and retain the positive time before rounding.
walkthrough:
Substitute the given condition $x = 80$ when $t = 25$ into the solution:
$$\ln 80 = -\dfrac{2}{3}k(25)\sqrt{25} + \ln 100$$
$$\ln 80 - \ln 100 = -\dfrac{2}{3}k(25)(5)$$
$$\ln\left(\dfrac{80}{100}\right) = -\dfrac{250}{3}k$$
$$\ln(0.8) = -\dfrac{250}{3}k$$

Express $t^{\frac{3}{2}}$ by taking the ratio with the equation for $t = 25$:
$$\dfrac{t^{\frac{3}{2}}}{25^{\frac{3}{2}}} = \dfrac{\ln(0.4)}{\ln(0.8)}$$
$$25^{\frac{3}{2}} = 25\sqrt{25} = 25 \times 5 = 125$$
$$t^{\frac{3}{2}} = 125 \times \dfrac{\ln(0.4)}{\ln(0.8)} \approx 125 \times \dfrac{-0.91629073}{-0.22314355} \approx 125 \times 4.1062837 \approx 513.2855$$

Solve for $t$ by raising to the power $\dfrac{2}{3}$:
$$t = (513.2855)^{\frac{2}{3}} = \left((513.2855)^{\frac{1}{3}}\right)^2 \approx (8.00669)^2 \approx 64.107$$
